classification: P1 functional: writing silently loses work when storage fails
screen_state: W-TASK-01 Draft; blocked localStorage or quota failure; leave task and return. Short lesson-writing uses a similar persistence pattern and belongs in regression scope, but the fresh data-loss reproduction is the extended task.
environment: Chromium, 390×844 storage fixtures; ordinary draft preservation also passed at 320,1366,844 with working storage.
reproduction: install either the blocked getter or failing `Storage.prototype.setItem` fixture from `scripts/states.py`; open task 01, choose Write, enter “Keep this draft”; leave to mode selection; reopen task 01 and Write.
expected: keep unsaved work in this session, clearly show saving is unavailable, and offer copying the draft before a destructive transition.
actual_impact: draft becomes empty on reopening during the same visit, with no task-level storage-failure notice. A child can lose an essay, not just a bookmark.
evidence: `storage.json` entries blocked/quota, with `draft_after_return: ""`; `UX-001-before-leaving.png` / `UX-001-after-return.png`. Working-storage control preserves text across mode/task switches and reload.
cause: confirmed save exception is swallowed and `start()` reloads task data from unavailable storage. Hypothesis to validate during correction: other task data and previously saved older content can exhibit the same loss/reversion pattern.
components_regression: `js/writing.js` load/save/start; plans, draft, checklist, scores, task isolation, reset, mode switching; inspect `js/skills.js` short-writing storage too.
recommendation_acceptance: retain per-task in-session fallback data, surface failure/success accurately, and protect unsaved writing. Both blocked and quota fixtures must preserve all task fields through leave/return; ordinary reload/task isolation/reset must still work. Do not promise persistence across browser close when storage is unavailable.

classification: P2 functional: a malformed nested progress record blocks lesson navigation
screen_state: Story elements `3.T.T.1.b`, Learn It → Watch Me, with a truthy primitive stored for that lesson.
reproduction: set `pp.progress.v1` to `{"3.T.T.1.b":true}`, load the app, open Story elements, click Watch Me.
expected: discard/recover the invalid lesson record and allow the tab change while preserving valid records elsewhere.
actual_impact: tab remains on Learn It; page error `Cannot create property 'taught' on boolean 'true'`. A damaged browser record can prevent study progression.
cause: confirmed outer-object validation accepts the map, but `rec(k)` trusts a truthy nested primitive; writing `taught` fails. Other malformed nested shapes are hypotheses until exercised.
components_regression: `js/skills.js` progress load/rec/mark and migration; existing scores, dates, adult observations, alternate-form history and retention flags.
recommendation_acceptance: normalize lesson records before use. Boolean/string/number/null/array fixtures must recover without page errors; valid neighboring scores/drafts remain unchanged; opening a screen must never invent a pass, date or Retained status.

classification: P2 instructional: graph explanation claims more than the data establish
environment: current source inventory and prior independent review; the item rendered at 320×568 and 1366×768. Explanation was inspected in source, not newly blind-solved.
reproduction: take/direct-open form B, submit, review the dwindled item explanation (or inspect its `why` string).
expected: explain the decrease in buckets picked, eight to four; make no inference about fruit remaining on trees.
actual_impact: says there were fewer pecans “left to pick.” The graph counts harvested buckets, so it cannot establish that claim. The key “became fewer” is correct; the explanation models an unsupported inference.
evidence: `source-inventory.json`, set `SK:3.L.V.3.a:tB`, item TB1; PP-004 final integration review's remaining feedback note.
cause: wording left from an earlier stem revision; revision history is not required to confirm the current mismatch.
components_regression: `js/data/lessons/L-V3.js`, TB1 explanation; graph alt/caption/stem/key and A/B score parity.
recommendation_acceptance: explain that fewer buckets were picked after week three. All words in feedback must follow from visible values; keep the correct key and points; inspect both forms and all hint/review presentations.

classification: P3 copy: counts below ten remain digits in instructional prose
screen_state: Try It Yourself launch, practice completion and blank-test confirmation.
environment: source plus fresh Try screen baseline screenshots and test confirmation/completion fixture coverage.
reproduction: open Story elements → Try It Yourself; read “3 new questions on your own”; submit a partly blank short check to view “You left … question(s)”; finish short practice for the dynamic completion sentence.
expected: spell out counts below ten in prose; retain standard codes, scores, percentages, question navigation and appropriate numbered steps.
actual_impact: generated prose interpolates digits. This breaks the agreed house style and makes copy inconsistent; it does not change scoring.
cause: confirmed direct numeric interpolation. PR #4 proposes a correction for Try's introductory count only; it is not part of main and does not resolve every dynamic prose location.
components_regression: lesson launch and player prose; singular/plural, zero through nine, ten or more; preserve numerical scores/codes/navigation.
recommendation_acceptance: apply the house style consistently to instructional counts, including dynamic empty/partial completion cases. Independently review PR #4's scope; no merge is implied by this report.
